summary: # Marvelous Designer Quick Start Tutorial - Fabric Attachments ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will explore how to attach fabrics in Marvelous Designer, including adjusting fabric properties and adding zippers. Follow along to enhance your workflow and achieve professional results. ## Selecting Fabric In the object window, select a type of fabric. In the attribute editor below, you can adjust the attributes of each fabric. 1. **Open Texture Image**: Click on the Open button next to the texture and browse to select the texture image you need. 2. **Texture Versions**: All versions of the fabric used will add textures. 3. **Adjust Texture Intensity**: By dragging the adjustment bar, you can increase the texture intensity to make it more prominent. 4. **Change Color and Transparency**: You can also modify the color and transparency of the fabric. 5. **Highlight Settings**: There are also highlight-related settings below. ## Fabric Properties In Marvelous Designer, different fabric textures are expressed by their physical properties. We have provided a variety of fabric previews to meet all kinds of needs. - **Fire-Resistant Fabrics**: Generally, fire-resistant fabrics are smoother. - **Wool Fabric**: When switching to wool fabric, the clothing appears harder. ## Production Process In the typical production process, clothes are made in the same way: 1. **Basic Sewing and Modeling**: Start with the default fabric for basic sewing and modeling. 2. **Modify Fabric Properties**: After completion, modify the fabric properties. ### Detail Properties Below, you can modify some detail properties: - **Stretching Performance**: The strength of the gold sand, tail sand, and diagonal line indicates the stretching performance of these fabric elements. The higher the value, the more difficult it is to stretch. - **Bending Strength**: This refers to how easy it is for the fabric to bend. A higher value means it's more difficult to bend the fabric. *Tip*: If you need to withdraw during the adjustment process, press Ctrl + Z. ## Adding Zippers Before adding a zipper, please delete the original sewing line. 1. **Delete Original Sewing Line**: Use the Edit Sewing Line function to select the sewing line and then press the Delete button. 2. **Simulation Gaps**: After opening the simulation, you might notice a gap between the panels. You can add a zipper. ### Creating the Zipper 1. **Select Zipper Tool**: After selecting the zipper tool, click on the starting point. 2. **Draw the Zipper**: Move the mouse in the direction of the zipper. At the end position, double-click to create a side zipper. The other side is operated in the same way. 3. **Aligning the Zipper**: Ensure that the two sides of the zipper are aligned. ### Simulation of the Zipper After starting the simulation, the zipper will attach itself, aligning correctly at the front. ## Adjusting Zipper Attributes When closing the simulation, use the move tool to select the zipper. You can type specific attributes in the parameter editor: - **Width, Thickness, and Particle Diameter**: Adjust these parameters as needed. - **Zipper Pattern and Color Transparency**: The lower part allows modification of the zipper pattern and transparency settings. - **Height Setting and Physical Attributes**: These can also be modified for more precise control. ### Modifying Zipper Head When selecting the head of the middle chain: 1. **Attribute Editor**: You can type its attributes in the attribute editor and modify its shape, proportion, and weight. 2. **Direction Selection**: When selecting the hook's direction for the chain cut, the chain will be cut from the other direction. 3. **Cancelling Selection**: If you cancel the hook selection, the chain will separate. ### Adjusting Chain Mechanism At this time, select to move to the reverse pull, and the chain head will appear on the other side. You can modify the strength, color, and other attributes of the chain head. ## Simulating the Chain When the hook is simulated, you can select and drag the chain head to adjust the position of the chain mechanism. During simulation, the chain will be pulled apart. ## Creating Strings Let's use the circuit divider to create a string on the panel line: 1. **Creating the String**: Click the starting point and continue to click along the line of the created string to prevent adding to other lines. At the end position, double-click to complete the string creation. 2. **Editing the String**: A string will appear on the panel line after completion. Use the tool to select the line to be edited. ### Editing Line Attributes After selecting the line, you can edit its width and particle diameter in the attribute editor. You can modify its fabric at the bottom. ## Changing Line Fabric After adding a type of fabric to the object window, you can change the line fabric from the drop-down menu. In the drop-down menu, adjust the width and particle diameter to match the object's specifications. 1. **Top Dropdown Effect**: Select and change the color at the top. 2. **Changing Effects**: Click on the drop-down menu at the bottom of the window to change the drop-down effect to yellow. 3. **Selecting Point Object**: Select the point object with the drop-down tool and press the ground arrow key. 4. **Bottom Object Selection**: After selecting the bottom object, click on the drop-down button to select the horizontal axis. You should notice the top of the icon has changed. --- This structured guide provides a comprehensive overview of fabric attachments in Marvelous Designer, ensuring that all essential details are preserved for effective learning and application.
